title: A good heart (Avot 2:9)
hook: Yochanan ben Zakkai asks his students the best path; the answer that wins is a good heart
carry: everything else grows from the heart
tomorrow: repent a day before you die

segments.voice: Yesterday, Hillel's chant: more things, more worry, more giving, more peace. Your line was more giving, more peace. Did you give something away? Day two hundred fifty-seven.

A teacher gives his five students one assignment. No test, no essay. Just: go out and look at the world, and come back and tell me the one good path a person should hold on to. Five students. Five answers. And then the teacher picks one, and explains why it wins. The teacher is Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai, the student of Hillel, remembered as the sage who kept Jewish learning alive when Jerusalem fell to Rome. And the winning answer is two Hebrew words: lev tov.
screen: `FIVE STUDENTS, ONE ASSIGNMENT.` → `YOCHANAN BEN ZAKKAI.` → `TWO WORDS WIN.`

segments.voice: Yochanan ben Zakkai says to his students: go out and see which is the good way a person should cling to. The five come back. Rabbi Eliezer says: a good eye, meaning a generous way of looking at people. Rabbi Joshua says: a good friend. Rabbi Yose says: a good neighbor. Rabbi Shimon says: someone who sees what's coming, who thinks about the results of what they do. And Rabbi Elazar ben Arach says: a good heart. Then the teacher speaks. I prefer the words of Elazar ben Arach, because his words include all of yours. Think about why. A good eye, generous seeing, starts in the heart. A good friend and a good neighbor are what a good heart becomes when it lives near people. Even seeing what's coming depends on caring about who gets hurt. The heart is the root, and the others are branches. In the Bible's Hebrew, the heart isn't just feelings. It's where a person thinks, decides and wants. So lev tov isn't only warmth. It's a whole inner life pointed toward the good. And then the Mishnah runs the same exercise backward. Yochanan asks: which is the bad way a person should stay away from? A bad eye, a bad friend, a bad neighbor, someone who borrows and doesn't pay back, and, from Elazar ben Arach again, a bad heart. And again the teacher says: his words include all of yours. Five answers, one root. Everything else grows from the heart.
screen: `GO OUT AND SEE THE GOOD WAY.` · `EYE, FRIEND, NEIGHBOR, FORESIGHT.` · `HIS WORDS INCLUDE ALL OF YOURS.` · `THE HEART IS THE ROOT.` · then, large: `LEV TOV: A GOOD HEART.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: tend the root. Settle, and breathe. Put a hand on your chest if that feels natural. Notice the heart going on quietly without you asking it to. Now think of the four branches. A good eye: someone you could see more generously. A good friend: someone you could reach out to. A good neighbor: someone near you who needs something. Foresight: one choice today whose results you could think through. Let each one come back to the heart. The bell holds the time.
Lev tov. A good heart: the answer Yochanan ben Zakkai chose, because it holds all the others inside it.
Your line: everything else grows from the heart. Today, before one decision, ask what a good heart would choose, and let the rest follow from that. Day two hundred fifty-seven.

screen: `DAY 257 COUNTS.` → `TOMORROW: REPENT A DAY BEFORE YOU DIE.`

howItsDone: This mishnah is studied as a portrait of character, and 'lev tov' is still an everyday Hebrew phrase for a kind, good-hearted person.

original.note: Hebrew: a good heart, still an everyday phrase in Israel.

trapdoor: what you thought: be a nice person.
what it means: a good heart is the root; a good eye, friend, neighbor and foresight grow from it.
what a scholar hears: in biblical Hebrew, lev is the seat of thought and will, not only of feeling.

notes: Avot is paraphrased (outline follows Taylor 1897). Numbering: 2:9 common, 2:13–14 in some editions.

'Kept Jewish learning alive when Jerusalem fell': the tradition of Yochanan ben Zakkai leaving besieged Jerusalem and founding the academy at Yavneh (Gittin 56a–b); phrased as 'remembered as'; confirm.
Rabbi Shimon's answer (ha-ro'eh et ha-nolad) is rendered 'someone who sees what's coming'; confirm.
The bad-way list includes 'one who borrows and does not repay' from Rabbi Shimon; confirm order.

Editor review: hook no longer opens 'Imagine'; 'five of his best students' is now 'his five students' (Avot 2:8 says he had five, not that they were his best); 'in the Torah' is now 'in the Bible's Hebrew'; howItsDone 'many Jews' removed.
